en: [Preceded by the *Kṣmādevī-stotra*] Homage to the glorious Śākyamuni!
I always bow to the Lion of the Śākyas, the Lord of Sages, who has come here for the sake of the Self-Existent One, accompanied by his assembly of disciples,
in order to perfectly illuminate the majesty of Sunepāla.
And likewise, he protected the people of Naiyapāla. || 1 ||
To protect Sudāsa’s son, the King of Kāśī— who,
due to a fault of his mother, was a man-eater wandering about—
and likewise a hundred sons of five kings.
Furthermore, the son of Soma became a practitioner of yoga. || 2 ||
Priya, the son of the King of Kāśi, a caravan leader who had obtained a wish-fulfilling gem during a voyage to the island of Vadadvīpa,
showered gold and other jewels, making [the city] rich in wealth.
He who does not bow to you has quickly brought ruin upon himself. || 3 ||
By offering his own flesh, he protected the dove; thus,
that son of a king named Mahāsattva became known as Sarvada, the best of protectors of the earth.
And I bow to you, O tigress, who have given birth along with your cub. || 4 ||
Having exerted great effort at Gayāśīrṣa for the sake of the world, he became Sarvārthasiddha;
having attained the enlightenment that is so difficult to find, he became a Buddha.
I bow to you in this existence; protect me, O Omniscient Lord! || 5 ||
Having praised and bowed at his lotus feet, she stood joyfully in a secluded spot with palms joined in reverence, full of longing to hear the description of Nepal.
Thus ends the hymn to the glorious Śākyasiṃha composed by the nun Cūḍā. May it be auspicious!

Oṃ dhīḥ! Svāhā to the victory over the Śruti and Smṛti!
Oṃ adhī huṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Oṃ gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate svāhā.
Oṃ, O Wisdom, O Great Wisdom, O Victory of Śruti and Smṛti, O Intelligence, svāhā!
The Noble Dhāraṇī of the Prajñāpāramitā Mantra is completed. May there be auspiciousness!
And a hymn:
Homage to the Perfection of Wisdom!
O Goddess Prajñā, who are non-conceptual, without support, blameless, and stainless; who are both eternal and non-eternal, and changeless—homage be to you! (1)
O Sovereign Mother of the Buddhas, Grandmother of the Bodhisattvas, Great-Grandmother of all sentient beings—O Goddess Prajñā, homage be to you! (2)
O Mother, O Mother, O Mother of the World—to you who grant the heart's desires, who are pure and wise, O Goddess, let there be salutation! 3.
O auspicious one, you are Lakṣmī; you are Śrī, Dhī, Śraddhā, Dhṛti, and Smṛti.
O Goddess, who are the embodiment of all, the sovereign of all, and supreme wisdom—salutations be unto you! (4)
O Goddess Prajñā, who consists of the ten perfections, both supramundane and mundane, and immeasurable—homage be to you! (5)
Thus ends the "Praise of the Perfection of Wisdom."
% [Followed by the Devatāsūtra]
